newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Shoemaker Bally denies eyeing Salamander.
newsitem.headline: Shoemaker Bally denies eyeing Salamander.

text.p: Bally, part of arms-to-fashion group Oerlikon-Buehrle Holding AG, denied media speculation that it planned to take over German shoemaker Salamander AG.
"We deny that Salamander is to be taken over," Bally spokesman Edwin van der Geest told Reuters when asked about a report in the German business newspaper Boersen-Zeitung.
The newspaper on Friday revived recent speculation that Salamander shareholders were planning an imminent change in the German group's ownership.
Major Salamander investors have denied plans to sell and Salamander said this week it did not know what its shareholders planned.

Bally is the shoes and fashion division of Oerlikon-Buehrle, whose other main businesses are military technology maker Oerlikon-Contraves and small aircraft builder Pilatus as well as Balzers and Leybold, a world leader in surface and vacuum technology.
